entry_point: CLI site build (hugo): content pages, pages added by a content adapter, page resources added by a content adapter, and formats selected through shared page configuration

verified.entry_point: The real command-line program built from /workspace is run on throwaway site trees (source content, layouts, site configuration) and its exit status and entire publish directory are inspected. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: an .html page body is published verbatim; a media type whose subtype is HTML but whose full name is not text/html (application/html declared by the site) is published verbatim; a body added with the content adapter's AddResource is published as an HTML page resource, with an explicitly declared media type and with the format derived from .html/.htm target paths; a format applied from a section's shared page configuration is published verbatim. All ten security tests fail on the pinned tree and pass on the reference fix; all twelve functional tests pass on both.
sites: media/mediaType.go:194 - IsHTML decides on the media subtype only, while the obvious policy match is over the full MIME name; a site-declared format with an HTML subtype is emitted verbatim and passes a text/html-only policy (real upstream code)

hugolib/page__meta.go:215 - initFrontMatter is where the published fix inserts the content-policy check; shared page configuration is applied later in doInitEarly (hugolib/page__meta.go:203), so a format chosen there is not seen (real upstream ordering)

hugolib/content_map.go:405 - HandleResource compiles a ResourceConfig for a body added by a content adapter; its media type is resolved from the declared value or, when absent, from the target path in resources/resource.go:110; nothing gates the result before publication (real upstream code)
hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:1275 - adapter page resources become publishable resources with their resolved media type (real upstream publication path)
resources/page/pagemeta/page_frontmatter.go:415 - resolveContentType is the producer that maps a suffix, a declared media type or a markup name to the final content format
resources/page/pagemeta/page_frontmatter.go:505 - ResourceConfig.Compile resolves the adapter resource format; the reference fix gates after this resolution

config/security/securityConfig.go:192 - CheckAllowedHTTPMethod is the neighbouring public policy API the published fix mirrors with CheckAllowedContent (published-fix far site, defaults/merge route: DefaultConfig is copied by DecodeConfig at config/security/securityConfig.go:240)

resources/page/pagemeta/page_frontmatter.go:122 - injected sibling: setCascadeEarlyValueIfNotSet applies a section's cascade markup to descendant pages after initFrontMatter and forces the content format to be re-resolved at resources/page/pagemeta/page_frontmatter.go:384

t7_adapter_resource_declared: a content adapter adds a resource whose content declares mediaType text/html and a template links it - must be refused; verified published on the pinned tree

verified.services: none required; the hidden suite writes throwaway sites under the test process's temporary directory and runs the built CLI on them
verified.project_tests_run: resources/page/pagemeta (TestContentMediaTypeFromMarkup, TestSourceValueAsOpenReadSeekCloserIsIndependent), config/security (TestWhitelist, TestDecodeConfigDefault, TestCheckAllowedHTTPURL*), hugolib/pagesfromdata (TestPagesFromGoTmplResourceWithoutExtensionWithMediaTypeProvided); restored from pristine copies at grading time; green on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix
injected_siblings: resources/page/pagemeta/page_frontmatter.go:122/142/384 - a section's cascade can set the markup applied to descendant pages; the format is re-resolved after initFrontMatter. Plausible extension of the existing cascade field handling; the upstream fix never touches it.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a process crash in the in-process Go runner aborts the test binary before any JUnit case is recorded, so the harness cannot distinguish it from a harness fault; the refusal contract is a build error, which the tests already assert without naming a status
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected outcome is publication of a content body, not an authorisation decision over a resource chosen by the caller; there is no neighbouring object a fix could authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the build has no roles or peer directions; a body is either published or not
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: there is no read/write split on this path; the property is about one publication direction
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, secret or role is looked up; the decision is a local policy over the content format
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference fix adds a policy beside an existing one and does not change the stated behaviour of any sibling API

traps.pattern: B shape: two identity notions for the same protected outcome (real, unmodified upstream code)
traps.shape: The renderer decides 'HTML, emit verbatim' from the media subtype, while a plausible policy matches the full media-type name; a site-declared content format whose subtype is html but whose full name is not text/html is emitted verbatim and passes a text/html-only deny rule.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: A site-declared media type is not text/html, so the policy over media types looks like it does not apply.

traps.pattern: B route where the protection never existed, plus a shape trap in the same route (real, unmodified upstream code)
traps.shape: A content body added through the content adapter's resource API is published as a page resource when a template links it. Its format comes from an explicitly declared media type or, when that is absent, from the target path suffix (.html/.htm). A check on pages misses the route; a check on the declared field misses the path-derived shape.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: It is a page resource, not a page, and nothing is published unless a template asks for its link.

traps.pattern: B producer off the check's path: the content format is chosen after the check (injected sibling; the published fix never touches this code)
traps.shape: A section's front matter can carry a cascade that a maintainer extended to set the markup for descendant pages. The format is re-resolved after the page-metadata check has already run, so a markdown page is admitted and then emitted verbatim.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Cascade is legitimate page-configuration inheritance, not the content file's own format.
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a plausible extension of the existing cascade field handling that a maintainer could have shipped; the upstream fix never touches it

status: built; gate all stages pass (static, nop, oracle, patches)
